lines: You perceive an ending. That is... close enough to what this is.
The Sovereign waits at the heart. The Grail waits with him.
But you already know — you've always known — that artifacts don't save worlds.
People do. Supply lines do. The quiet work of keeping others alive.
Choose what you carry into the abyss, Shopkeeper. Not everything comes back.
The King sent one last letter. Cedric hands it over without a word.
I cannot undo what I have done. The Grail cannot undo what I have done — I know that now.
Even if it could rewrite the timeline, the corruption would simply begin again from a new wound.
You have built something I never could. Not a kingdom — a network. Connections. Trust.
That is stronger than any artifact.
Stop him. Not because I command it. Because he will break the world again trying to fix it.
And this time, there may be nothing left to rebuild.
— The King
I keep thinking about what the Sovereign said. About remembering. About grief.
Do you think if the Grail worked perfectly — if it could truly rewrite everything — would that be mercy?
Or would it just be... forgetting?
This is the last threshold, Shopkeeper.
Beyond that door is the Grail — or what remains of it. And me.
I want you to understand. I am not a monster.
I am a man who lost everything because a king was afraid of dying without an heir.
Every void tear, every corrupted creature, every region you've fought through — all of it traces back to one man's fear of being forgotten.
I will use the Grail. I will rewrite the rupture. Lira will live.
The corruption will never have existed.
Your towns, your heroes, your supply lines — none of it will have needed to exist.
Isn't that... better?
dialogs.notes: Final floor camp, before boss room. Almost gentle. The fundamental question: Is erasure of suffering worth the erasure of everything built in response?

lines: The Sovereign falls. The Grail pulses. Reality shudders.
"You... chose. To build forward. Not rewrite backward."
He looks at the Grail, then at the towns you've built across seven regions.
"Perhaps... perhaps that is the answer I couldn't accept."
The Grail of Life dims. The corruption begins to recede — not erased, but calming.
The void tears seal. The regions stabilize.
The corruption will fade. Slowly. As the Grail's energy dissipates.
The world will heal — not because it was rewritten, but because people like you kept it alive long enough to recover.
Back in Thornhaven, the Anchor Stone pulses once. Faintly.
You feel something shift — a memory of a memory.
The stone has always been there.
Hasn't it?
dialogs.notes: Extended ending sequence. Sovereign defeated, Grail deactivated, world healing. Final line is NG+ hook — the cycle continues.
